subs.title: Number of Solutions and Solutions in an Interval
Trigonometric Inequalities, Range and Related Identities

questions.q: If \(\tan\theta=-\dfrac43\) then \(\sin\theta\) is
questions.sol: \(\theta\) is in the second quadrant (\(\sin\theta=\frac45\)) or the fourth (\(\sin\theta=-\frac45\)).

questions.q: If \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=2\pi\) then
questions.sol: \(\frac\alpha2+\frac\beta2+\frac\gamma2=\pi\), and for \(A+B+C=\pi\): \(\tan A+\tan B+\tan C=\tan A\tan B\tan C\).

questions.q: The equation \(2\cos^2\dfrac x2\sin^2x=x^2+\dfrac1{x^2}\), \(x\le\dfrac\pi9\) has
questions.sol: LHS \(\le2\) and RHS \(\ge2\), with RHS \(=2\) only at \(x=\pm1\), where LHS \(=2\cos^2\frac12\sin^21<2\).

questions.q: The solution of \(\sin x+\cos x=1\) is
questions.sol: \(\sin\left(x+\frac\pi4\right)=\frac1{\sqrt2}\), so \(x+\frac\pi4=n\pi+(-1)^n\frac\pi4\).

questions.q: The general solution of \(\sin x-3\sin2x+\sin3x=\cos x-3\cos2x+\cos3x\) is
questions.sol: \(\sin2x(2\cos x-3)=\cos2x(2\cos x-3)\) and \(2\cos x\ne3\), so \(\tan2x=1\).

questions.q: The equation \((\cos P-1)x^2+(\cos P)x+\sin P=0\) in the variable \(x\), has real roots. Then \(P\) can take any value in the interval,
questions.sol: \(D=\cos^2P+4(1-\cos P)\sin P\ge0\) certainly when \(\sin P\ge0\), i.e. for every \(P\in(0,\pi)\); in the other intervals it can be negative (e.g. \(P=-\frac\pi2\) gives \(D=-4\)).

questions.q: In a triangle \(ABC\), angle \(A\) is greater than angle \(B\). If the measure of angles \(A\) and \(B\) satisfy the equation \(3\sin x-4\sin^3x-k=0\), \(0<k<1\), then the measure of angle \(C\) is
questions.sol: \(\sin3A=\sin3B=k\) with \(A\ne B\): \(3A=\pi-3B\), so \(A+B=\frac\pi3\).

questions.q: The number of solutions of the equation \(\sin(e)^x=5^x+5^{-x}\) is
Let \(n\) be a positive integer such that \(\sin\dfrac\pi{2n}+\cos\dfrac\pi{2n}=\dfrac{\sqrt n}2\). Then
questions.sol: For \(n>1\), \(1<\sin\frac\pi{2n}+\cos\frac\pi{2n}=\sqrt2\sin\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi{2n}\right)<\sqrt2\) (equality only at \(n=2\), which does not satisfy the equation; \(n=1\) fails too). So \(1<\frac{\sqrt n}2<\sqrt2\). (In fact \(n=6\).)

questions.q: The general values of \(\theta\) satisfying the equation \(2\sin^2\theta-3\sin\theta-2=0\) is
questions.sol: \((2\sin\theta+1)(\sin\theta-2)=0\), so \(\sin\theta=-\frac12=\sin\frac{7\pi}6\).

questions.q: Let \(n\) be an odd integer. If \(\sin n\theta=\sum\limits_{r=0}^nb_r\sin^r\theta\), for every value of \(\theta\), then
questions.sol: \(\theta=0\) gives \(b_0=0\). Dividing by \(\sin\theta\) and letting \(\theta\to0\): \(b_1=\lim\dfrac{\sin n\theta}{\sin\theta}=n\).

questions.q: The number of values of \(x\) in the interval \((0,5\pi)\) satisfying equation \(3\sin^2x-7\sin x+2=0\) is
questions.sol: \(\sin x=\frac13\) (as \(\sin x=2\) is impossible): two solutions in each of \((0,\pi)\), \((2\pi,3\pi)\), \((4\pi,5\pi)\).

questions.q: Which of the following numbers are rational?
questions.sol: \(\sin15^\circ\cos15^\circ=\frac12\sin30^\circ=\frac14\). The others are \(\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2\sqrt2}\), \(\frac{\sqrt3+1}{2\sqrt2}\) and \(\sin^215^\circ=\frac{2-\sqrt3}4\).

questions.q: In a triangle \(PQR\), \(\angle R=\dfrac\pi2\). If \(\tan\left(\dfrac P2\right)\) and \(\tan\left(\dfrac Q2\right)\) are the roots of the equation \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) \((a\ne0)\) then
questions.sol: \(\frac P2+\frac Q2=\frac\pi4\): \(\dfrac{-b/a}{1-c/a}=1\), i.e. \(-b=a-c\).

questions.q: The maximum value of \((\cos\alpha_1)\cdot(\cos\alpha_2)\ldots(\cos\alpha_n)\) under the restrictions \(0\le\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_n\le\dfrac\pi2\) and \((\cot\alpha_1)\cdot(\cot\alpha_2)\ldots(\cot\alpha_n)=1\) is
questions.sol: \(\prod\cos\alpha_i=\prod\sin\alpha_i\), so \(\left(\prod\cos\alpha_i\right)^2=\prod\dfrac{\sin2\alpha_i}2\le\dfrac1{2^n}\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha+\beta=\pi/2\) and \(\beta+\gamma=\alpha\), then \(\tan\alpha\) equals
questions.sol: \(\tan\alpha\tan\beta=1\) and \(\tan\gamma=\tan(\alpha-\beta)=\dfrac{\tan\alpha-\tan\beta}2\).

questions.q: Then number of integral values of \(k\) for which the equation \(7\cos x+5\sin x=2k+1\) has a solution is
The values of \(\theta\in(0,2\pi)\) for which \(2\sin^2\theta-5\sin\theta+2>0\), are
questions.sol: \((2\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta-2)>0\) and \(\sin\theta-2<0\), so \(\sin\theta<\frac12\).

questions.q: For \(x\in(0,\pi)\), the equation \(\sin x+2\sin2x-\sin3x=3\) has
questions.sol: LHS \(=\sin x\left[2+4\cos x-4\cos^2x\right]=\sin x\left[3-(2\cos x-1)^2\right]\le3\), with equality only if \(\sin x=1\) and \(\cos x=\frac12\) together — impossible.

questions.q: Let \(S=\left\{x\in(-\pi,\pi):x\ne0,\pm\dfrac\pi2\right\}\). The sum of all distinct solutions of the equation \(\sqrt3\sec x+\text{cosec}\,x+2(\tan x-\cot x)=0\) in the set \(S\) is equal to
questions.sol: Multiplying by \(\sin x\cos x\): \(\sqrt3\sin x+\cos x=2\cos2x\), i.e. \(\cos\left(x-\frac\pi3\right)=\cos2x\). So \(x=\frac{2n\pi}3+\frac\pi9\) or \(x=2n\pi-\frac\pi3\): \(x=\frac\pi9,\frac{7\pi}9,-\frac{5\pi}9,-\frac\pi3\), which add to \(0\).

questions.q: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be a function defined by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2\sin\left(\dfrac\pi{x^2}\right),&\text{if }x\ne0,\\0,&\text{if }x=0.\end{cases}\) Then which of the following statements is TRUE?
opts: \(f(x)=0\) has infinitely many solutions in the interval \(\left[\dfrac1{10^{10}},\infty\right)\).
\(f(x)=0\) has no solutions in the interval \(\left[\dfrac1\pi,\infty\right)\).
The set of solutions of \(f(x)=0\) in the interval \(\left(0,\dfrac1{10^{10}}\right)\) is finite.
\(f(x)=0\) has more than \(25\) solutions in the interval \(\left(\dfrac1{\pi^2},\dfrac1\pi\right)\).
questions.sol: For \(x>0\): \(f(x)=0\) iff \(x=\frac1{\sqrt n}\), \(n=1,2,3,\ldots\) (a) needs \(n\le10^{20}\): finitely many. (b) \(n\le\pi^2\): \(n=1,\ldots,9\) are solutions. (c) \(n>10^{20}\): infinitely many. (d) \(\pi^2<n<\pi^4\): \(n=10,\ldots,97\), i.e. \(88\) solutions.

questions.q: Let \(2\sin^2x+3\sin x-2>0\) and \(x^2-x-2<0\) (\(x\) is measured in radians). Then \(x\) lies in the interval
questions.sol: \((2\sin x-1)(\sin x+2)>0\) gives \(\sin x>\frac12\); \(x^2-x-2<0\) gives \(-1<x<2\). In \((-1,2)\), \(\sin x>\frac12\) for \(\frac\pi6<x<2\) (as \(\frac{5\pi}6>2\)).

questions.q: For a positive integer \(n\), let \(f_n(\theta)=\left(\tan\dfrac\theta2\right)(1+\sec\theta)(1+\sec2\theta)(1+\sec4\theta)\ldots(1+\sec2^n\theta)\) then
questions.sol: \(\tan\frac A2(1+\sec A)=\dfrac{\sin\frac A2}{\cos\frac A2}\cdot\dfrac{2\cos^2\frac A2}{\cos A}=\tan A\). Repeating, \(f_n(\theta)=\tan(2^n\theta)\), and each given value is \(\tan\frac\pi4=1\).

questions.q: For \(0<\theta<\dfrac\pi2\), the solution(s) of \(\sum\limits_{m=1}^6\text{cosec}\left(\theta+\dfrac{(m-1)\pi}4\right)\text{cosec}\left(\theta+\dfrac{m\pi}4\right)=4\sqrt2\) is(are)
questions.sol: Each term is \(\sqrt2\left[\cot\left(\theta+\frac{(m-1)\pi}4\right)-\cot\left(\theta+\frac{m\pi}4\right)\right]\); the sum is \(\sqrt2\left[\cot\theta-\cot\left(\theta+\frac{3\pi}2\right)\right]=\sqrt2(\cot\theta+\tan\theta)\). So \(\dfrac2{\sin2\theta}=4\), \(\sin2\theta=\frac12\).

questions.q: Solve : \(2(\cos x+\cos2x)+(1+2\cos x)\sin2x=2\sin x\), \(-\pi\le x\le\pi\).
questions.sol: Using \(\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x\) and dividing by \(2\): \(\cos x+\cos2x+\sin x\cos x+\sin x\cos2x=(1+\sin x)(\cos x+\cos2x)=0\). \(\sin x=-1\): \(x=-\frac\pi2\). \(2\cos^2x+\cos x-1=0\): \(\cos x=\frac12\) or \(-1\).

questions.q: Prove that \(5\cos\theta+3\cos\left(\theta+\dfrac\pi3\right)+3\) lies between \(-4\) and \(10\).
questions.sol: It equals \(\frac{13}2\cos\theta-\frac{3\sqrt3}2\sin\theta+3\), and \(\sqrt{\frac{169}4+\frac{27}4}=7\). So the value lies in \([3-7,3+7]\).

questions.q: For all \(\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac\pi2\right]\) show that \(\cos(\sin\theta)\ge\sin(\cos\theta)\).
questions.sol: \(\sin\theta+\cos\theta\le\sqrt2<\frac\pi2\), so \(0\le\cos\theta<\frac\pi2-\sin\theta\le\frac\pi2\). As sine increases on \(\left[0,\frac\pi2\right]\): \(\sin(\cos\theta)<\sin\left(\frac\pi2-\sin\theta\right)=\cos(\sin\theta)\).

questions.q: Find the coordinates of the points of intersection of the curves \(y=\cos x\) and \(y=\sin3x\) if \(-\dfrac\pi2\le x\le\dfrac\pi2\).
questions.sol: \(\sin3x=\sin\left(\frac\pi2-x\right)\): \(3x=\frac\pi2-x+2n\pi\) gives \(x=\frac\pi8+\frac{n\pi}2\) (\(\frac\pi8,-\frac{3\pi}8\)); \(3x=\frac\pi2+x+2n\pi\) gives \(x=\frac\pi4+n\pi\) (\(\frac\pi4\)).

questions.q: Show that \(e^{\sin x}-e^{-\sin x}=4\) has no solution.
questions.sol: With \(y=e^{\sin x}\): \(y^2-4y-1=0\), \(y=2\pm\sqrt5\). \(2-\sqrt5<0\) and \(2+\sqrt5>e\ge e^{\sin x}\): no real \(x\).

questions.q: Find all solutions of \(4\sin x\cos^2x-2\sin^2x=3\sin x\).
questions.sol: \(\sin x\left[4(1-\sin^2x)-2\sin x-3\right]=0\): \(\sin x=0\) or \(4\sin^2x+2\sin x-1=0\), \(\sin x=\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt5}4=\sin\dfrac\pi{10}\) or \(\sin\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{10}\right)\).

questions.q: Find all the solutions of \(2^{1+|\cos x|+|\cos x|^2+\ldots\infty}=4\) in \((-\pi,\pi)\)
questions.sol: The exponent is \(\dfrac1{1-|\cos x|}=2\), so \(|\cos x|=\frac12\).

questions.q: Show that \(2\sin x+\tan x\ge3x\), where \(0\le x<\dfrac\pi2\)
questions.sol: \(f(x)=2\sin x+\tan x-3x\), \(f'(x)=\cos x+\cos x+\sec^2x-3\ge3\sqrt[3]{\cos x\cdot\cos x\cdot\sec^2x}-3=0\) (AM–GM). So \(f\) is increasing and \(f(0)=0\).

questions.q:
Prove that for any positive integer \(k\), \(\dfrac{\sin2kx}{\sin x}=2[\cos x+\cos3x+\cos5x+\ldots+\cos(2k-1)x]\)
Hence prove that \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin2kx\cdot\cot x\,dx=\dfrac\pi2\)
questions.sol:
\(2\sin x\cos(2r-1)x=\sin2rx-\sin(2r-2)x\); adding for \(r=1,\ldots,k\) gives \(\sin2kx\).
Then \(\sin2kx\cot x=2\cos x\sum\cos(2r-1)x=\sum[\cos2rx+\cos(2r-2)x]\). Over \(\left[0,\frac\pi2\right]\) every \(\cos2mx\) (\(m\ge1\)) integrates to \(0\), and the single constant term \(1\) (from \(r=1\)) gives \(\frac\pi2\).

questions.q: Determine the smallest positive value of \(x\) (in degrees) for which \(\tan(x+100^\circ)=\tan(x+50^\circ)\tan(x)\tan(x-50^\circ)\)
questions.sol: Write it as \(\dfrac{\tan(x+100^\circ)}{\tan x}=\tan(x+50^\circ)\tan(x-50^\circ)\) and apply componendo–dividendo: \(\dfrac{\sin(2x+100^\circ)}{\sin100^\circ}=\dfrac{\cos100^\circ}{-\cos2x}\). So \(2\sin(2x+100^\circ)\cos2x=-\sin200^\circ\), i.e. \(\sin(4x+100^\circ)=-\sin200^\circ-\sin100^\circ=-\cos50^\circ=\sin220^\circ\). Smallest positive \(x\): \(4x+100^\circ=220^\circ\).

questions.q: Find the smallest positive value of \(p\) for which \(\cos(p\sin x)=\sin(p\cos x)\) has a solution \(x\in[0,2\pi]\).
questions.sol: \(\cos(p\sin x)=\cos\left(\frac\pi2-p\cos x\right)\) gives \(p(\sin x\pm\cos x)=2n\pi\pm\frac\pi2\). Since \(|\sin x\pm\cos x|\le\sqrt2\), we need \(p\sqrt2\ge\frac\pi2\).

questions.q: Find all values of \(\theta\) in the interval \(\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\) satisfying the equation \((1-\tan\theta)(1+\tan\theta)\sec^2\theta+2^{\tan^2\theta}=0\)
questions.sol: With \(u=\tan^2\theta\ge0\): \((1-u)(1+u)+2^u=0\), i.e. \(2^u=u^2-1\), satisfied by \(u=3\) (and by no other \(u\ge0\)). So \(\tan\theta=\pm\sqrt3\).

questions.q: Prove that the value of the function \(\dfrac{\sin x\cos3x}{\sin3x\cos x}\) do not lie between \(\dfrac13\) and \(3\) for any real \(x\).
questions.sol: \(y=\dfrac{\tan x}{\tan3x}=\dfrac{1-3t^2}{3-t^2}\) with \(t=\tan x\), so \(t^2=\dfrac{3y-1}{y-3}>0\), i.e. \(y<\frac13\) or \(y>3\).

questions.q: There exists a solution of \(\theta\) between \(0\) and \(2\pi\) that satisfies the equation \(\sin^4\theta-2\sin^2\theta-1=0\).
questions.sol: \(\sin^2\theta=1\pm\sqrt2\), neither of which lies in \([0,1]\).

questions.q: The larger of \(\cos(\log\theta)\), and \(\log(\cos\theta)\) if \(e^{-\pi/2}<\theta<\dfrac\pi2\) is ........
questions.sol: \(-\frac\pi2<\log\theta<\log\frac\pi2<\frac\pi2\), so \(\cos(\log\theta)>0\); and \(0<\cos\theta<1\) makes \(\log(\cos\theta)<0\).

questions.q: The solution set of the equations \(x+y=\dfrac{2\pi}3\), \(\cos x+\cos y=\dfrac32\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are real is .....
questions.sol: \(\cos x+\cos y=2\cos\frac\pi3\cos\frac{x-y}2=\cos\frac{x-y}2\le1<\frac32\).

questions.q: General values of \(\theta\) satisfying the equation \(\tan^2\theta+\sec2\theta=1\) are .................
questions.sol: With \(t=\tan^2\theta\): \(t+\dfrac{1+t}{1-t}=1\) gives \(t(t-3)=0\).

questions.q: The real roots of the equation \(\cos^7x+\sin^4x=1\) in the interval \((-\pi,\pi)\) are ................. and ............
questions.sol: \(\cos^7x\le\cos^2x\) and \(\sin^4x\le\sin^2x\), so the sum is \(\le1\) with equality only if \(\cos x\in\{0,1\}\): \(x=0,\pm\frac\pi2\).

questions.q: If \(\cos(x-y)\), \(\cos x\) and \(\cos(x+y)\) are in H.P., then \(\cos x\sec\left(\dfrac y2\right)=\) ....................
questions.sol: \(\cos x=\dfrac{2\cos(x-y)\cos(x+y)}{2\cos x\cos y}\) gives \(\cos^2x\cos y=\cos^2x-\sin^2y\), so \(\cos^2x=1+\cos y=2\cos^2\frac y2\).

questions.q:
Paragraph
Let \(f(x)=\sin(\pi\cos x)\) and \(g(x)=\cos(2\pi\sin x)\) be two functions defined for \(x>0\). Define the following sets whose elements are written in the increasing order :
\(X=\{x:f(x)=0\}\), \(Y=\{x:f'(x)=0\}\), \(Z=\{x:g(x)=0\}\), \(W=\{x:g'(x)=0\}\)
List-I contains sets \(X,Y,Z\) and \(W\). List-II contains some information regarding these sets.
List-IList-II
(I) \(X\)(P) \(\supseteq\left\{\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac{3\pi}2,4\pi,7\pi\right\}\)
(II) \(Y\)(Q) an arithmetic progression
(III) \(Z\)(R) NOT an arithmetic progression
(IV) \(W\)(S) \(\supseteq\left\{\dfrac\pi6,\dfrac{7\pi}6,\dfrac{13\pi}6\right\}\)
(T) \(\supseteq\left\{\dfrac\pi3,\dfrac{2\pi}3,\pi\right\}\)
(U) \(\supseteq\left\{\dfrac\pi6,\dfrac{3\pi}4\right\}\)
Which of the following is the only correct combination?
questions.sol: \(X\): \(\cos x\in\{0,\pm1\}\), \(x=\frac{n\pi}2\) — an A.P. containing \(\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2,4\pi,7\pi\): (P), (Q). \(Y\): \(\sin x=0\) or \(\cos x=\pm\frac12\), i.e. all multiples of \(\frac\pi3\): (Q), (T). \(Z\): \(\sin x=\pm\frac14,\pm\frac34\): (R). \(W\): \(\cos x=0\) or \(\sin x\in\{0,\pm\frac12,\pm1\}\): \(\frac\pi6,\frac\pi2,\frac{5\pi}6,\pi,\ldots\) — not an A.P., contains the sets in (P) and (S): (P), (R), (S).

questions.q:
Consider the following lists
List-IList-II
(I) \(\left\{x\in\left[-\dfrac{2\pi}3,\dfrac{2\pi}3\right]:\cos x+\sin x=1\right\}\)(P) has two elements
(II) \(\left\{x\in\left[-\dfrac{5\pi}{18},\dfrac{5\pi}{18}\right]:\sqrt3\tan3x=1\right\}\)(Q) has three elements
(III) \(\left\{x\in\left[-\dfrac{6\pi}5,\dfrac{6\pi}5\right]:2\cos(2x)=\sqrt3\right\}\)(R) has four elements
(IV) \(\left\{x\in\left[-\dfrac{7\pi}4,\dfrac{7\pi}4\right]:\sin x-\cos x=1\right\}\)(S) has five elements
(T) has six elements
The correct option is :
questions.sol: (I) \(x=0,\frac\pi2\). (II) \(3x\in\left[-\frac{5\pi}6,\frac{5\pi}6\right]\) with \(\tan3x=\frac1{\sqrt3}\): \(3x=\frac\pi6,-\frac{5\pi}6\). (III) \(2x=\pm\frac\pi6,\pm\frac{11\pi}6,\pm\frac{13\pi}6\) (all within \(\pm\frac{12\pi}5\)): six. (IV) \(x=\frac\pi2,\pi,-\frac{3\pi}2,-\pi\): four.

questions.q: The number of values of \(\theta\) in the interval \(\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\) such that \(\theta\ne\dfrac{n\pi}5\) for \(n=0,\pm1,\pm2\) and \(\tan\theta=\cot5\theta\) as well as \(\sin2\theta=\cos4\theta\) is
questions.sol: \(\tan\theta=\cot5\theta\) gives \(\cos6\theta=0\): \(\theta=\pm\frac\pi{12},\pm\frac\pi4,\pm\frac{5\pi}{12}\). \(\sin2\theta=1-2\sin^22\theta\) gives \(\sin2\theta=\frac12\) or \(-1\): \(\theta=\frac\pi{12},\frac{5\pi}{12},-\frac\pi4\). All three are common.

questions.q: The maximum value of the expression \(\dfrac1{\sin^2\theta+3\sin\theta\cos\theta+5\cos^2\theta}\) is
questions.sol: The denominator is \(3+2\cos2\theta+\frac32\sin2\theta\), with minimum \(3-\frac52=\frac12\).

questions.q:
Two parallel chords of a circle of radius \(2\) are at a distance \(\sqrt3+1\) apart. If the chords subtend at the centre, angles \(\dfrac\pi k\) and \(\dfrac{2\pi}k\), where \(k>0\), then the value of \([k]\) is
[Note : \([k]\) denotes the largest integer less than or equal to \(k\)].
questions.sol: The chords are at distances \(2\cos\frac\pi{2k}\) and \(2\cos\frac\pi k\) from the centre, on opposite sides: \(\cos\frac\pi{2k}+\cos\frac\pi k=\frac{\sqrt3+1}2\), satisfied by \(\frac\pi{2k}=\frac\pi6\), \(k=3\).

questions.q: The positive integer value of \(n>3\) satisfying the equation \(\dfrac1{\sin\dfrac\pi n}=\dfrac1{\sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}n\right)}+\dfrac1{\sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}n\right)}\) is
questions.sol: With \(a=\frac\pi n\): \(\dfrac{\sin3a-\sin a}{\sin a\sin3a}=\dfrac1{\sin2a}\) gives \(2\cos2a\sin2a=\sin3a\), i.e. \(\sin4a=\sin3a\), so \(4a=\pi-3a\).

questions.q: The number of distinct solutions of the equation \(\dfrac54\cos^22x+\cos^4x+\sin^4x+\cos^6x+\sin^6x=2\) in the interval \([0,2\pi]\) is
questions.sol: \(\cos^4x+\sin^4x=1-\frac12\sin^22x\), \(\cos^6x+\sin^6x=1-\frac34\sin^22x\). The equation becomes \(\cos^22x=\sin^22x\), i.e. \(\cos4x=0\): \(x=\frac\pi8+\frac{n\pi}4\), \(8\) values.

questions.q: Let \(a,b,c\) be three non-zero real numbers such that the equation \(\sqrt3a\cos x+2b\sin x=c\), \(x\in\left[-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right]\), has two distinct real roots \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with \(\alpha+\beta=\dfrac\pi3\). Then, the value of \(\dfrac ba\) is _____ .
questions.sol: Subtracting the equations for \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) and dividing by \(2\sin\frac{\alpha-\beta}2\): \(-\sqrt3a\sin\frac{\alpha+\beta}2+2b\cos\frac{\alpha+\beta}2=0\), so \(\dfrac ba=\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\tan\dfrac\pi6=\dfrac12\).

questions.q:
Match each entry in List-I to the correct entry in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) The number of elements in the set \(\{x\in[-\pi,\pi]:\sin^6x+\cos^4x=1\}\)(1) is \(1\)
(Q) The number of elements in the set \(\left\{x\in\left[-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right]:\sin^2x+\cos^6x=1\right\}\)(2) is \(2\)
(R) The number of elements in the set \(\left\{x\in[-\pi,\pi]:\cos^2\left(\dfrac x2\right)-\sin^2x=\dfrac12\right\}\)(3) is \(3\)
(S) The number of elements in the set \(\left\{x\in[-2\pi,2\pi]:6\sin^2\left(\dfrac x2\right)-\cos3x=3\right\}\)(4) is \(4\)
(5) is \(5\)
questions.sol: (P) With \(s=\sin^2x\): \(s(s-1)(s+2)=0\): \(x=0,\pm\pi,\pm\dfrac\pi2\). (Q) \(\cos^2x(\cos^4x-1)=0\): \(x=0,\pm\dfrac\pi2\). (R) \(2\cos^2x+\cos x-2=0\): \(\cos x=\dfrac{\sqrt{17}-1}4\), two values of \(x\). (S) \(3(1-\cos x)-\cos3x=3\) gives \(\cos^3x=0\): \(x=\pm\dfrac\pi2,\pm\dfrac{3\pi}2\).

questions.q:
Question Stem
Consider the curve \(C_1\) given by \(y=e^{-x}\) for \(x\in[0,10\pi]\), and the curve \(C_2\) given by \(y=e^{-x}(\sin x+\cos x)\) for \(x\in[0,10\pi]\).
Let \(n\) be the total number of points of intersection of the curves \(C_1\) and \(C_2\).
Suppose that \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_n\in[0,10\pi]\) are the \(x\)-coordinates of the points of intersection of the curves \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) such that \(\alpha_1<\alpha_2<\cdots<\alpha_n\).
The value of \(n\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(\sin x+\cos x=1\): \(x=2k\pi\) or \(x=2k\pi+\dfrac\pi2\). In \([0,10\pi]\): \(0,2\pi,\ldots,10\pi\) (six) and \(\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac{5\pi}2,\ldots,\dfrac{17\pi}2\) (five).
